bull.b: Operating expense reductions and sequential adjusted EBITDA improvement show that management’s cost actions are beginning to improve operating efficiency. If maintained as revenue scales, these actions could support progress toward the company’s stated goal of positive adjusted EBITDA.

Expansion beyond RV demand into heavy-duty trucking and Dakota Lithium’s specialty battery markets broadens the company’s customer base and distribution reach. These channels create additional routes for revenue growth and may reduce reliance on a single end market over time.

Additional patent protection strengthens Dragonfly’s intellectual-property position in dry-electrode and solid-state batteries. A broader protected technology portfolio can support differentiation, improve strategic partnership prospects, and preserve potential long-term advantages in advanced energy storage.

bear.b: Large ongoing losses and deeply negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued cash consumption can restrict investment capacity, increase reliance on financing, and make the company more vulnerable if operating improvements take longer than expected.

Revenue contraction alongside weaker RV shipments shows that Dragonfly remains exposed to softness in a core end market. Lower demand can delay operating leverage, reduce absorption of fixed costs, and make the path to the company’s profitability target dependent on newer channels ramping successfully.

The stockholders’ equity deficiency creates a material corporate and financing risk because failure to regain Nasdaq compliance could lead to delisting. Reduced access to public markets would make it harder to raise equity capital, support liquidity, and fund the company’s growth initiatives.
